page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.8xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory is provisioned at 64 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 480 MB of shared L3 cache. Hardware accelerators are not bundled, as the instance features zero GPUs. Network capabilities consist of an 8 Gbps baseline throughput, and no local ephemeral storage is attached to the host.

The underlying processor features Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) supporting bfloat16 and int8 formats, alongside Advanced Vector Extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-VNNI. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via AES-NI, VAES, and SHA-NI flags. Memory protection and system integrity are maintained through Total Memory Encryption (TME) and Indirect Branch Restricted Speculation (IBRS).

Benchmark metrics reflect strong capability in compute-heavy execution threads. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved 2153.0 in single-core and 17709.0 in multi-core routines, with text processing scoring in the top decile. In PassMark, the CPU registered an aggregate score of 51553.17 with strong physics and encryption results. Data compression benchmarks also place the platform in the top quartile, reaching 33.95 GB/s in single-threaded gzip and 222.99 GB/s in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Small-scale model inference using a 135M model yielded 2512.5 prompt tokens per second. Conversely, memory bandwidth across uncached 256 MB blocks and synthetic database operations remain within middle 50 percent industry distributions.

The flex tier architecture incorporates burstable CPU resource allocation, which offers qualitative cost-efficiency advantages over fixed-compute instances when handling variable utilization patterns. However, the absence of onboard NVMe storage requires external network block storage for persistence. Given its architectural strengths in integer manipulation, vector extensions, and DDR5 throughput, c8i-flex.8xlarge is practical for static web serving, batch data compression, CPU-based machine learning inference, and text processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance implements burstable CPU allocation and is paired with 64 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AMX-BF16, and AMX-INT8, which support accelerated mathematical operations and integer computation. The server provides 8 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes zero dedicated local storage, relying on external network volumes. In benchmark testing, the hardware demonstrates strong performance in compression routines, text processing, and small-scale language model inference, while memory bandwidth and database operations deliver midrange throughput. Because of its burstable allocation model, it provides qualitative resource cost advantages for compute workloads with variable demands, such as static web serving, text data processing, and batch tasks.
